body.statement: Under exact donor-span identification and the fixed singular gap, \[\sqrt K\begin{pmatrix}\widehat\theta-\theta\\ \widehat s_1-s_1\end{pmatrix}=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}+o_P(1)\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta).\] The influence vectors are those in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence}; their plug-in estimates obey \(K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2=o_P(1)\), and \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\). This limit law applies under covariate-dependent censoring satisfying conditional independence and does not replace \(\theta\) by a marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-target.
body.justification: The theorem supplies the first joint root-\(K\) law for a censoring-adjusted spectral survival counterfactual and its factual comparator.
body.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorem 2) give finite-sample consistency under non-informative censoring, while Westling et al. (2024, Theorem 2) have no data-dependent spectral transport; neither result contains this joint influence vector.
body.consumer: The theorem provides standard errors for the untreated United States curve and its contrast with observed single-agent therapy in the TCL analysis.
